calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Penguins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Panthers are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Hot take: the Penguins break through anyway.
calls.call: The Penguins’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Panthers.

calls.body: It’s the Panthers’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Penguins get more of the play than usual.

calls.head: Forecheck against patience
calls.body: On forecheck pressure, Florida is the league’s best, but Pittsburgh is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect the Panthers to win more pucks back deep in the Penguins’ end.
calls.call: The Panthers put more forecheck pressure on than the Penguins.

surprises.head: Florida’s kill smothered Pittsburgh’s power play
surprises.body: Florida has one of the league’s stingiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a dry night: Pittsburgh’s power play created 1.5 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.2 (about 6.5 against Florida) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

surprises.head: A shutout for Artūrs Šilovs
surprises.body: Šilovs stopped all 26 shots, worth 2.1 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 15 starts.

story.head: Šilovs slams the door on the Panthers
paras: The Panthers’ Cooper Black made his NHL debut in net. Nick Robertson got the scoring started for the Penguins late in the first, and Hendrix Lapierre made it 2-0 midway through the second. Evgeni Malkin stretched the lead to 3-0 early in the third. Robertson scored his second of the night into the empty net with two and a half minutes left.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Artūrs Šilovs, who gave up five goals in Utah in his last start, stopped all 26 shots for the Penguins.
Neither power play scored: the Penguins killed all four Panthers power plays, and the Panthers killed all three of Pittsburgh’s. The Pens moved to 4-6-1, and the Panthers dropped to 5-4-2.

items.text: The Penguins won for the first time in five games.
Evgeni Malkin extended his point streak against Florida to seven games.
Sidney Crosby’s six-game point streak against Florida ended.
Matthew Tkachuk’s nine-game point streak ended.
